label: late original-phase position (8th/9th original token)
explanation: Position counter for the late original phase. Fires only on original-phase input steps at orig_idx >= 6. It is active on 96% of orig_idx 7 steps and 100% of orig_idx 8 steps; orig_idx 6 fires on about 31% of steps, weakly; orig_idx 5 fires on about 1%. Magnitude rises with position: orig_idx 8 steps hold 42% of the mass on half as many steps as orig_idx 7, and the top examples are all at step 8. The input token identity barely matters (lift at most 1.9x per token). Firing at orig_idx 6 is somewhat more likely when the token is a first occurrence or when the sequence has more digits. It never fires at orig_idx <= 4, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase. So it is effectively silent for L <= 6. Predicate orig_idx >= 7 on dev: P 0.97, R 0.75, F1 0.84, mass recall 0.90. The misses are the weak orig_idx 6 activations.

issues: The positional claims hold up. The unit is active at orig_idx 7 on 95.7% of steps and at orig_idx 8 on 100%. At orig_idx 6 it is active on 31%, at orig_idx 5 on 1.1%, and at orig_idx 4 on only 6 steps. It is silent on the delimiter and throughout the copy phase. The test scores reproduce: P 0.970, R 0.750, F1 0.846, mass recall 0.904.

The claim that token identity barely matters is false. The marginal in_tok lift (at most 1.9x) hides strong token gating once you condition on position. At orig_idx 6 the firing rate depends heavily on the input token: j 98%, r 95%, a 72%, k 67%, h 65%, 3 62%, l 58%, p 57%, but w 0%, u 0.3%, q 1.9%, 0 1.9%, t 2.3% and e 6.5%. So the 'weak orig_idx 6 misses' are mostly a token-dependent class, not noise.

The predicate has a systematic false-positive class: orig_idx 7 with in_tok == 'w' fires on only 31% of 1119 steps, against 98% for other tokens. This class accounts for most of the predicate's false positives. u (79%), t (90%) and q (91%) at orig_idx 7 are also low.
The claim that orig_idx 6 firing is more likely on first occurrences is not supported. The rate is 31.0% when in_first=1 and 32.3% when in_first=0. The n_digits effect is negligible (33% vs 31%).
Length of the sequence (L) does not change the orig_idx 6 rate (31% for L=7, 8 and 9). So the unit counts absolute position, not distance to the delimiter. This part of the label is fine.
